# Chromes and captions

The program's colors come in two built-in kinds, each chosen on its own.

- A **chrome** is one of Cool Edit Pro 2.1's own color presets. It colors the waveform and its canvas, the grid and center lines, the markers, the playhead, and the Panel Face that the toolbar, the panels round the waveform, the menus, the dialogs and the cards are all drawn from.
- A **caption** is a Windows color scheme of the period, of which the title bar's colors alone are used: the title, its gradient end and its text, and the same three for a window without the focus.

To choose one, open the Settings menu and pick Chrome or Caption: the Settings line opens on the key in use. Type another key from the lists below (Tab completes a typed beginning) and press OK or Enter: it applies at once and is kept for the next launch. Cancel or Esc leaves the colors as they were. A word that is no preset's key is refused.

The defaults: the chrome Default (`cool-edit-default`) and the caption Windows Storm (`windows-storm`).

## Chromes

Cool Edit Pro 2.1's twenty color presets, in Cool Edit's own order, as their text stands inside its program file (coolpro.exe). Two of them carry no name there; 3D and Easy on the Eyes are their names in Cool Edit's own registry entries.

- Classic Cool records no Panel Face, so Cool Edit follows Windows' button face for it: here it takes Default's Face, the program's default chrome.
- The waveform's outline is not one of Cool Edit's colors: each chrome's is its waveform color darkened, the same hue at a fixed lightness.
- The Invalid color, which marks an invalid marker, is each chrome's own center-line color.
- The scanner (the line that moves during playback) and the zoom's anchor line are white in every chrome, as Cool Edit's scanner is on every one of its presets.

## Captions

The 42 captions are the Windows color schemes of the period, grouped by where they come from.

### Windows

The Appearance schemes of Windows 95, 98, 2000 and Me. Most are Windows 2000's and Windows XP's classic schemes as ReactOS's setup data records them, checked against the same schemes saved from Windows XP's Display Properties as .theme files, which are also the source of Desert, Spruce and Windows 98 Standard; Windows 2000 Standard is Windows 2000's own setup data; Windows 95 Standard and the six Windows 95 schemes are the Windows 95 CD's own (shell2.inf).

- The Windows 95 CD carries 27 Appearance schemes. Only the six whose colors differ from Windows 2000's of the same name are listed, as Windows 95 Maple, Wheat, Marine, Storm, Rose and Plum; the other 21 are equal to a scheme listed here (Windows Standard, Brick, Spruce, Teal, Red, White, and Blue, Pumpkin, Eggplant, Rainy Day, Desert, Lilac, Slate), a size variant of one, or a high-contrast scheme.
- Windows Me Standard is Windows 2000 Standard's colors: Windows Me changed only the font.
- ReactOS's own "ReactOS Standard" and "ReactOS Classic" are Windows 2000 Standard and Windows 98 Standard under other names, listed under those.
- Windows 98's own default scheme records no title-bar gradient; Windows 98 Standard's gradient is the one Windows 2000 and Windows XP record for the same scheme.
- A scheme that records no gradient (every Windows 95 one) draws its title bar in one flat color.

### Windows 98 and Plus! desktop themes

The color schemes of the desktop themes Windows 98 and Microsoft Plus! shipped, from their own .theme files.

- The names leave out the themes' color-depth tag, "(256 color)" or "(high color)".
- None of the themes records a title-bar gradient: their title bars are one flat color.
